menu.settings.dev.benchmark.description: Closes the menu and runs the standard benchmark packages, then shows the results.
menu.settings.dev.consoleoverlay.descrip: Draws console output over the game, so you can read it without opening the console.
menu.settings.dev.consoleoverlay.title: Console Overlay
menu.settings.display.fov.description: How wide the default camera sees, in degrees. Games are free to override this with their own.
menu.settings.display.fps.description: The ceiling while you're in a game. 0 is uncapped. A limit a little under your refresh rate keeps frame pacing steadier than letting it run free.
menu.settings.display.fps_inactive.descr: The ceiling while the window isn't focused. Low is usually right - it gives the machine back to whatever you alt-tabbed to.
menu.settings.display.fps_menu.descripti: The ceiling while you're in the menu rather than a game. There's rarely a reason for the menu to run as hard as a game.
menu.settings.display.mode.description: Borderless fills the screen at your desktop resolution and alt-tabs instantly. Exclusive takes the display outright, which can shave a frame of latency but is slower to leave.
menu.settings.display.resolution.descrip: How many pixels the game is drawn at. Borderless always uses the desktop resolution, so this only applies to the other two window modes.
menu.settings.display.vsync.description: Waits for the display before showing a frame. Removes tearing at the cost of some latency, and caps you to the refresh rate.
menu.settings.dlss_unavailable: DLSS isn't available on this device. Choose another option.
menu.settings.every_upscaler_renders_to_: Every upscaler renders to a target that can't be multisampled, so this has no effect while one is on.
menu.settings.game.chat.description: Turns the platform chat off everywhere, including in games that use it.
menu.settings.game.language.description: The language the menu and any game that's been translated is shown in.
menu.settings.game.streamer.description: Hides names and anything else personal that would otherwise end up on a stream.
menu.settings.gfx.aa.description: Multisampling on geometry edges. Without it foliage and hair fall back to a hard cutout, so 2x is worth having.
menu.settings.gfx.ao.description: Contact shading in creases and where objects meet. Levels raise trace quality and go from quarter, to half, to full resolution. The dearest effect here.
menu.settings.gfx.bloom.description: Light bleeding out of bright pixels. Costs very little.
menu.settings.gfx.aa_modes.description: CMAA2 smooths the finished image and costs very little. MSAA smooths geometry edges and costs more as samples go up. CMAA2 can add samples on top.
menu.settings.gfx.dlss_quality.descripti: Which render resolution DLSS works from. DLAA runs at native resolution and spends the whole budget on image quality instead.
menu.settings.gfx.dof.description: Blurs whatever a game marks as out of focus. Levels add blur samples. Costs nothing unless a game asks for it.
menu.settings.gfx.fog.description: Light scattering through fog and smoke. Levels raise the fog volume from 60x40x32 up to 320x200x128, which is the bulk of the cost.
menu.settings.gfx.fsr1_sharpness.descrip: How hard FSR sharpens the upscaled image. Too much makes edges crunchy.
menu.settings.gfx.fsr3_quality.descripti: Which render resolution FSR3 works from. Native still runs the temporal pass, so it's anti-aliasing rather than upscaling.
menu.settings.gfx.fsr3_sharpness.descrip: How hard FSR3 sharpens the upscaled image.
menu.settings.gfx.motionblur.description: How far the blur smears. 0 stops motion blur even in games that ask for it.
menu.settings.gfx.motionblur_quality.des: Levels take 4, 12 or 16 samples along movement. Cheap either way; strength decides whether it blurs at all.
menu.settings.gfx.postprocess.descriptio: Sets every effect below in one go.
menu.settings.gfx.shadows.description: Shadow map resolution, how far the sun casts, and how many lights cast at all. One of the heaviest settings on a busy scene.
menu.settings.gfx.ssr.description: Reflects on-screen geometry off glossy surfaces. Levels trace at a quarter, half, then full resolution, and the cost climbs with them.
menu.settings.gfx.texture.description: Resolution textures stream in at, plus anisotropic filtering. Costs video memory rather than frame time, so lower it if you're short on VRAM.
menu.settings.gfx.water.description: Wave mesh detail and the resolution of the view through the surface. Higher levels use finer waves and sharper captures, and High adds planar reflections where a map uses them.
menu.settings.gfx.upscaler.description: Renders below display resolution and scales up. The cheapest frame rate you can buy, at a visible cost to sharpness, worst on text and fine detail.
menu.settings.gfx.upscaler_scale.descrip: Share of display resolution the scene is drawn at. Lower is faster and softer.
menu.settings.graphics.blurb: How much the scene costs to draw.
